title: Regular Polygon Area Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Geometry
description: Change the number of sides and the size of a regular polygon to see how its apothem, perimeter, and area are related by A = ½aP, and how the polygon approaches a circle.

educational.topic: Area of regular polygons, apothem, and perimeter
learningObjectives: Students will be able to calculate the area of a regular polygon with A = ½aP and analyze how the apothem, the perimeter, and the number of sides affect the area.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with a visual derivation of the formula from congruent triangles
keyQuestions: Why is the apothem the height of each triangle?
What happens to the apothem as the number of sides increases while the radius stays fixed?
Why does the polygon's area approach πr²?
commonMisconceptions: The apothem and the radius are the same segment (the apothem ends at the midpoint of a side, the radius at a vertex).
More sides always means a much larger area (for a fixed radius the area is bounded by the circle).
The formula works for any polygon (it requires a regular polygon).
assessmentOpportunities: Given a regular octagon with apothem 6.93 units and side length 5.74 units, students compute the perimeter and the area, then predict whether a regular 12-gon with the same radius has a larger or smaller area and justify the prediction.
